articles.title: DoctorSpeak: Why anaemia is a threat to women of all ages
articles.description: Meera (52), a schoolteacher, had been feeling unusually tired for months. She found it difficult to concentrate, and often felt dizzy or breathless while climbing stairs. She attributed these changes to menopause and her busy lifestyle. During a routine check-up, her haemoglobin (Hb) was found to be 7.8 g/dL (normal levels are between 11 and 14). Further evaluation revealed iron deficiency caused by prolonged heavy menstrual bleeding during her perimenopausal years. With iron therapy, diet changes and treatment, her Hb improved, and so did her energy levels.
